item.title: Portfolio Watch — the FDA opened a pre-IND rolling-review pilot whose eligibility description is Blackbird's operating model, and applications close October 30th: Operation TrialBlazer's Expedited IND Pilot pairs a drug sponsor with a Qualified Research Institution — an academic medical center, which for us means Johns Hopkins or U-M-B — and reviews individual IND components on a rolling basis during the pre-IND phase, 8 to 10 pairs in the first cohort, with CBER's Karim Mikhail naming reduced clinical-hold risk as the objective, which is exactly the thread running through Biohaven, REGENXBIO and the summer AAV holds; candid limits are that 8-10 slots is a lottery and the RFI-stage design had QRI review advisory only with the 30-day clock unchanged; plus GSK buying a PRECLINICAL trispecific T cell engager from China's Chimagen for up to $750M, which drops the ex-US comparator ladder below the $45M/$75M/$110M clinical rungs to the exact stage a Blackbird asset is sold at, with an upfront neither side would print where the same pair disclosed $300M two years ago — and a read that cuts our way, since GSK's autoimmune engager bet from that same seller is B-CELL depletion while Winnow is antigen-specific T-cell redirection; AstraZeneca's SERENA-4 missing in first-line breast cancer, which means the version of camizestrant needing no diagnostic does not work and the ctDNA-guided indication approved on September 4th is not a carve-out but the entire franchise, revising our own September 7th read upward while making the assay's value contingent on one sponsor's one accelerated approval; GeneDx and Beren funding free sequencing for Niemann-Pick type C, where 475 American children are believed affected and 175 are diagnosed, which says our GJB2 number is a prevalence figure and patient-finding is a cost line we own; and Cullinan and Taiho filing in first-line lung cancer with three treatment-related septic-shock deaths, which prices the benefit-risk trade in oncology and inverts hard for an autoimmune engager
item.description: The Blackbird Brief Portfolio Watch for Tuesday, September 15, 2026. Recency window 2026-09-11 to 2026-09-15. LEAD — On 2026-09-15 the FDA opened applications for the Expedited IND Pilot Program under Operation TrialBlazer, the HHS roadmap launched 2026-06-22 to keep early clinical research in the US. Federal Register notice 2026-06-24, Docket FDA-2026-N-4699; comments closed 2026-08-24; it is now taking applications, which close 2026-10-30. Mechanism: a drug sponsor pairs with a Qualified Research Institution — academic medical center, CRO, or health system with relevant scientific depth — and the pair applies jointly, after which FDA reviews and accepts individual IND components on a rolling basis during the PRE-IND phase rather than waiting for a complete submission. Initial cohort 8-10 sponsor-QRI pairs; selection and launch Q4 2026. CDER director Michael Davis described rolling acceptance of individual components during the pre-IND phase; CBER director Karim Mikhail said the goal is to identify and resolve issues earlier, reduce the risk of clinical holds, and make the path to first-in-human trials more predictable; Acting Commissioner Kyle Diamantas said the pilot tests whether the partnership also accelerates what happens after the FDA allows a trial to proceed. Why it is ours: every Blackbird program sits in this window — nonprofit grant, de-risked academic asset, spinout, first IND, with Aletira, NuGate and the GPR52 NewCo all pre-IND — and the QRI half of the application is Johns Hopkins, UMB or Hopkins Medicine, counterparties we already hold grant relationships with. Against the running clinical-hold thread (Biohaven's partial hold between signing and closing on a $350M licence over nonclinical data the buyer had seen; REGENXBIO; the summer AAV holds), the most expensive event available to a Blackbird asset before first patient is a hold on the FIH protocol. Candid limits: 8-10 slots against the whole US industry is a lottery, so an application is cheap optionality rather than a plan; and as described at the RFI stage QRI pre-review was advisory only, with FDA keeping full decision authority and the 30-day IND clock unchanged, so confirm the shape before committing a program. Companion: the PDUFA VIII public meeting is 2026-09-16 for fiscal years 2028-2032, where FDA has proposed a 50% NDA fee reduction (~$2.3M) for products with early-stage US trials — Ovid CEO Jeremy Levin's critique that the incentive arrives near the end of development but must influence decisions made years earlier is exactly the argument for TrialBlazer, which arrives at pre-IND. Also in that docket, a push for a standing cross-functional Rare Disease Regulatory Science and Review capability inside FDA. ACTION: decide this week whether we apply, with which program and which institution. ITEM 2 — GSK is acquiring a PRECLINICAL trispecific T cell engager from Chimagen Biosciences (Chinese; Shanghai and Chengdu, founded 2016; platform spanning cancer and autoimmune disease) for up to $750M, full global rights, undisclosed upfront plus milestones, Phase 1 expected 2027. Every prior rung on the ex-US comparator ladder had a molecule characterised against a clinical or near-clinical bar — DualityBio $45M upfront for discovery through Phase 1a, Simcere $75M early-clinical, HUTCHMED $110M Phase 1, Solstice/Harbour $50M cash for Phase 2-ready. This one has never been in a person, which drops the comparator to the exact stage a Blackbird asset is sold at, and leaves the 09-13 conclusion standing: the only differentiator worth claiming is an unencumbered composition-of-matter position. Flagged as inference, not fact: the upfront was not printed where the same buyer and seller disclosed $300M upfront in 2024, and an undisclosed upfront is usually a small one. Second read, and it cuts our way — GSK's autoimmune engager bet from this same seller is CMG1A46, a CD19xCD20 TCE in Phase 1 for B-cell-dependent autoimmune disorders. That is B-CELL DEPLETION. Winnow is antigen-specific T-cell redirection. B-cell depletion in autoimmunity is crowded; antigen-specific T-cell targeting is not, and that belongs in the first paragraph of the Winnow deck. ITEM 3 — AstraZeneca's SERENA-4 Phase 3 missed its primary PFS endpoint: camizestrant plus palbociclib versus anastrozole plus palbociclib in upfront first-line ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer, no biomarker selection, numerical improvement only. Susan Galbraith said it sharpens their focus on maximising the patients who can benefit based on SERENA-6; Leerink cut peak sales from ~$2.9B to ~$830M; analysts had given it ~20% probability of success. On 09-07 we filed the Guardant360 longitudinal CDx as having got its indication as a passenger on AstraZeneca's Phase 3. Eight days later the version of the drug needing no diagnostic failed, so the molecularly guided indication is not a niche carve-out of a large franchise — it IS the franchise, and the assay is the reason there is a product. That is a stronger precedent for the Artemyx monitoring thesis than we credited. The harder half: it makes the diagnostic's entire value contingent on one sponsor's one trial, and SERENA-6 is an accelerated approval with a confirmatory trial still owed, so Artemyx must be inside more than one sponsor's protocol-design conversation. ITEM 4 — GeneDx (Gaithersburg, MD) and Beren Therapeutics launched NPC GenomeComplete for Niemann-Pick disease type C: no-cost testing, no insurance, targeted NPC1/NPC2 variant testing with 48-hour urgent results, fully financed by Beren, which is developing adrabetadex for the same disease. Roughly 475 US children are believed to have infantile-onset NPC; about 175 carry a diagnosis. Two-thirds are unidentified and the therapeutic sponsor is paying for the search. Read for Aletira: "GJB2 is ~200,000 people US+EU" is a prevalence figure, and the operative number is how many carry a confirmed molecular diagnosis. Newborn hearing screening detects hearing loss; it does not genotype anyone, and Skylark's SONIX requires confirmed biallelic GJB2 variants, so patient identification already rate-limits a ten-child study. Two questions: what fraction of severe-to-profound congenital SNHL carries a molecular diagnosis, and who pays for that panel. If the answers are "a minority" and "nobody," patient-finding is a cost line we own and belongs in the Series A budget. ITEM 5 — Cullinan and Taiho will file zipalertinib in first-line EGFR exon-20-insertion NSCLC off Phase 3 REZILIENT3 (n=280): PFS 14.5 versus 8.5 months, ~50% risk reduction, interim OS benefit 28% — with three septic-shock deaths in the treatment arm determined by the companies to be related to the study regimen, and grade 3+ adverse events 87% versus 54.4%. William Blair called the efficacy robust. Beside Saturday's Scholar Rock approval on two nominal p-values, the pattern is that current review discretion runs on magnitude of benefit, not cleanliness of the safety table. The inversion is ours: Winnow's indications do not kill on a six-month clock, so there is no survival delta available to purchase that tolerance with, and the safety table is not a section of the package but the product. Quiet: nothing on Clasp, GPR52/Nxera, NuGate, Biolinco or 1104health; no fresh otology or AAV-selectivity readouts.
